pipeline_protocol: Logical CPU 2; Windows thread cycles; three warmups; separate untimed allocation probe; seven batches; four alternating processes per version. Requested iterations are three, with at least 64 for readers up to 65536 native bytes and 2048 for other outputs below 4096 bytes. Complete native samples/palettes and independently modeled filtered bytes are checked outside timing. Fingerprints identify exact PNG input bytes.
checkpoint_scope_note: Freeze-only checkpoint records retain the shared driver's default 12-iteration scope description but contain no timed outputs. Every paired manifest and TSV records the actual three-iteration request and per-case minimum.
fixture_scope: Stored noise and compressed repeating gradients cover native gray/GA/RGB/RGBA at 8/16 bits, indexed8, small packed gray1/2/4, plain/Adam7, Paeth controls, 1x1 tails and large plain RGBA8/16. Complete PNG APIs return native samples and palette values. Both compression modes are timed except the largest 4097x257 controls, which use Stored.
in_process_protocol: Immutable Git baseline and selected crate link into one executable with shared native image types and copied optimized/LTO bench settings. All 188 API case/operations check complete native samples and palettes before timing. Three processes each retain eleven alternating batches per variant after one warmup. Small cases use 512 iterations; large cases three. Timed calls black-box the complete Png result in each branch.
retained_components: Fixed-channel reader pixel copies sharing the existing buffered scatter kernel
Reserved plain image output appended row by row, omitting full-image zero initialization
Power-of-two streaming history capped by output limit and 32768 bytes
history_invariant: A legal distance cannot exceed produced bytes or the RFC window. Produced bytes never exceed the configured output limit. The rounded history therefore covers every legal back-reference; larger streams keep the original 32768-byte ring. The history length stays fixed after construction, including zero-limit streams.
test_changes: Add independent flate2 known answers around output-limit powers of two, including fragmented reads/writes, exact prefix consumption and too-small limits. Replace old height-independent memory equality with a bounded-growth/saturation check and remove obsolete lower bounds requiring more than 32768 bytes from the boundary test and shared resource fuzzer helper. The first validation run found the shared lower bound and is preserved in final-validation.json/final-tests.log. Sample/error/event assertions and independent fixture generators remain intact.
serialization: Our builds, benchmark processes and correctness jobs are serialized. Other host workloads, CPU frequency and preemption are uncontrolled. All component and control measurements remain recorded; small timing differences are not treated as established gains.
shared_image_checkout: The unchanged shared deadlib-image/src/lib.rs checkout uses CRLF while Git stores LF. Audit normalizes this known checkout difference; PNG source matches Git bytes directly.
report_checksum: The report digest describes Git-normalized LF text; a CRLF working checkout is equivalent. Raw measurement, source-manifest and executable digests retain exact bytes.
allocation_expectations: Allocation calls and reallocations do not increase. Reader history requested bytes decrease only when the rounded output limit is below 32768. Plain append removes initialization work but keeps the full final-image reservation. Interlaced output remains initialized for pass scatter.
